messages:
maria: Heads-up — customer CUST-4218 opened a ticket at 10:28 UTC reporting API p95 ~2s in sa-east, a bunch of 504s. They say it started ~10:20 and is intermittent. Anyone seeing platform alarms?
jon: Not seeing global alerts. Any trace IDs or examples from the user?
maria: They pasted trace id trace-9f3a. Quick sample curl from their env shows connect+ttls ~1800ms. Link to ticket: https://support.redwood.ai/t/CUST-4218
priya: Pulling edge telemetry now. Correlating with our route-change audit — we did a GSLB reweight at 10:15 UTC to shift traffic for SA->US for cap bump. Could be related.
priya: Quick network check from our probe in sa-east:
```
$ traceroute api.redwood.com -m 12
1  sa-pop-1 (10.0.1.1)  2.3 ms
2  transit-peer-3  18.7 ms
3  us-gw-proxy  210.4 ms
4  us-interconnect  212.1 ms
5  api-redwood-frontend  214.0 ms
```
(we're seeing an unexpected path via us-gw-proxy for some sessions)
jon: That explains extra RTT. Is DNS resolving to the US anycast addresses or is it a post-DNS internal reroute?
priya: Looking at DNS logs: sa-east clients' A records were resolving to sa-pop VIPs until ~10:14. After GSLB change they started resolving to us-pop VIPs for ~28% of queries. TTL was 30s for the sa-pop record (we lowered it during the reweight to allow fast rollbacks). Short TTL + weight change = churn.
priya: Also TLS session reuse stats from sa-pop show cache miss spike around 10:18 — so sessions are being created to new frontends (cold TLS + cert handshake adds ~150-250ms). Combined with cross-region hop -> p95 increase.
maria: Customer reported many 504s from multiple devices, likely client-side timeouts hitting while waiting on TLS/connect.
tom: Can we roll back the GSLB weights to pre-change value? That should steer traffic back to sa-pop quickly once TTLs expire.
priya: Rolling back now. I also bumped the sa-pop weight to prefer; should take effect within 30s TTL window.
priya: mitigation note: changed TTL back to 300s after rollback to reduce churn while we investigate.
deploy-bot: route-audit: GSLB weight change rollback applied by priya @ 3176543280.
jon: From infra side, let's also pre-warm TLS caches on sa-pop for the next hour and re-seed KV caches for hot customer prefixes so cold starts don't amplify p95. I can push the pre-warm job.
priya: Pre-warm job kicked off. Will monitor p95/p99.
maria: I replied to the customer letting them know we identified an unintended traffic shift after a GSLB reweight and that we're rolling back. Asked for any additional traces.
jon: After rollback metrics: 10:31–10:38 we see p95 back down from ~1800ms to ~320ms for sa-east traffic. 504 rate dropped to baseline.
priya: Action items: 1) Root cause = low-TTL GSLB reweight created DNS churn and sent ~30% SA traffic to US POPs; cross-region hops + cold TLS/KV caused p95 spike. 2) Immediate mit = rollback weights, increase TTL, pre-warm TLS/KV. 3) Follow-up = change playbook: require canary monitoring and soft-threshold on DNS churn for future GSLB changes; consider automated session warmers for reweights.
maria: Customer updated ticket to say perf improved, will keep open for 24h.
jon: Marking postmortem not required (short lived, mitigated <20m) but we should add a runbook note under eng-sre/gslb for TTL guidance.
priya: Adding runbook snippet now.
tom: +1 on runbook and also recommend an automated gate that refuses GSLB weight changes that would route >20% cross-region without approval.
priya: Noted. If anyone sees residual 5xxs ping me.
maria: thanks all :thumbsup:
